audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL-related specs: DID authentication RPC methods (EIP-2844), Ethereum Provider API (EIP-1193), block hash log filtering (EIP-234), EOF metadata sections (EIP-7834), and eth/69 protocol changes (EIP-7642).

misclassified_entities.reason: From EIP-1193: 'Wallet/Client' is described as trusted software that processes RPC requests. In the context of the Provider API, the Wallet is the system under audit's backend, not an external entity. The DApp is the external entity.

From EIP-1193: 'Ethereum Network' is too generic. The actual external entity is the P2P peer nodes providing network connectivity. The network itself is an abstraction, not a concrete entity sending data.

From EIP-1193: 'Wallet User' is the human operator controlling the wallet. They interact via the wallet UI, not via a system boundary. User consent is an internal wallet process, not an external data flow.
From EIP-7834: 'Verification Tool' (e.g., Etherscan) reads on-chain data post-deployment. It does not send data INTO the EL. It is a consumer of EL state, not a trust boundary source.
From EIP-7834: 'Contract Deployment Source' (compiler/tool) submits EOF bytecode via transactions. The actual external entity is the transaction submitter via JSON-RPC, not the compiler itself.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via Ethereum Provider API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-1193 and EIP-2844: DApps are untrusted web applications calling Provider methods. They may be malicious, attempting to trick users into signing transactions or granting excessive permissions. All request parameters must be validated and sensitive operations require user consent.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client via eth_getLogs/eth_newFilter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-234: External applications query logs via JSON-RPC. Unauthenticated interface. Parameters must be validated (mutual exclusivity of blockHash and fromBlock/toBlock, hash format). Resource-intensive queries could be used for DoS.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via eth/69 Protocol
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth/69 Status handshake, BlockRangeUpdate, GetReceipts messages
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-7642: Peers exchange status and history range information over unauthenticated P2P. Peers may lie about block ranges, provide invalid receipts, or spam BlockRangeUpdate messages. All peer-provided data must be validated independently.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp Client via DID RPC Methods
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-2844: DApps request DID authentication and signing operations. Nonces must be validated for replay protection. Path-based permissions must be enforced. Auto-decryption must only apply to pre-approved paths.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All request arguments must be validated. Rate limiting must be enforced. Provider must not expose private data. Provider-Wallet isolation must be maintained. Sensitive operations (signing, account access) require explicit user consent.

Mutual exclusivity of blockHash and fromBlock/toBlock must be enforced. Block hash format must be validated (32-byte hex). Block lookup must handle non-existent hashes gracefully. Query resource consumption must be bounded.

Peer status must be validated for networkid, genesis hash, and forkid compatibility. Block range claims must be verified by attempting actual data retrieval. BlockRangeUpdate frequency must be rate-limited to prevent spam. Receipt data received without bloom filters must have blooms recomputed and validated against receipt root.

Nonces must be validated for freshness and uniqueness to prevent replay attacks. Path-based permissions must be strictly enforced. Auto-decryption only for authenticated path prefixes. JWS creation requires proper DID key resolution. All cryptographic operations must use secure implementations.
